name: dynamic-networks
title: Dynamic Networks — a catalog of network-reconfiguring rules
description: This investigation is a catalog: each study instantiates the same generalized process with a different registered reaction and shows the network evolving under that rule as an interactive animation and a GIF. Family A (studies 1–8) covers the dynamics OF networks — rules that rewire topology. A later Family B will add continuous multi-species dynamics ON the networks (an SBML simulator at each node via viva-copasi, with transport/diffusion along edges).
lead: Network science has many models of how graphs grow and rewire, usually studied one at a time. Here they become a single reusable machine: a process-bigraph process whose structural reactions are swapped to produce each dynamic, so the whole family is directly comparable — same substrate, same metrics, same visualization — and extensible with one new reaction per new rule.

at_a_glance.role: Null baseline — random growth, no hubs (Poisson degrees).
Fitness-weighted growth → a latecomer can overtake old hubs (Bianconi–Barabási).
Opinions + rewiring co-adapt → like-minded clusters (Gross–Blasius); bridge to Family B.
Activity-driven firing → a blinking temporal network (Perra).
Family B: a Repressilator (SBML) at each node + protein diffusion along edges → synchronisation.
Family B control: diffusion off (D=0) → oscillators stay out of phase.
Family C (synthesis): SBML reactors run while forest-fire growth BUILDS the network — most newcomers entrain; sync is topology-dependent.
Family C: reactors on a ring whose edges are continuously rewired — synchrony survives the changing wiring.
Proposed: couple via one diffusible signal molecule (quorum sensing) instead of all proteins.
Proposed: swap the Repressilator for a Brusselator to show the node model is a plug-in.
Proposed: let the continuous SBML state drive the rewiring — the continuous analogue of study 07.

glossary.definition: A structural rewrite of the bigraph emitted as _add/_remove sentinels on a map port; here it adds/removes network nodes and edges.
Number of edges incident to a node.
A network whose degree distribution has a power-law tail — a few very-high-degree hubs.
High local clustering with short global path lengths.
Edge count growing super-linearly in node count as a network evolves.

biological_story: Networks are everywhere in biology — protein interactions, gene regulation, metabolism, neurons, ecological webs — and they are not static. This investigation treats the *rules* that reshape a network as the object of study. Duplication-divergence (study 5) is the explicit genome-evolution analogue: a gene duplicates, the copy inherits its partners, then diverges by losing some — reproducing the heavy-tailed, clustered topology of real protein-interaction networks. Preferential attachment and fitness capture how some nodes become hubs. Adaptive coevolution (study 7) is the conceptual bridge to the next phase: when the state ON the nodes feeds back on the wiring between them. Family B makes that concrete: a COPASI/SBML Repressilator runs in every node and its proteins diffuse along the edges, so connected oscillators entrain — continuous, multi-species reaction–diffusion dynamics ON the network.
question: How do different local rules reshape a network over time, and can a single process-bigraph process — driven by pluggable reactions — reproduce the canonical families of network dynamics, each with a clear visualization of the network evolving?
hypothesis: One generalized NetworkDynamicsProcess, reconfiguring a graph through process-bigraph _add/_remove structural reactions, can reproduce the signature topology of every classic dynamic-network model — random growth, preferential attachment, small-world rewiring, fitness, duplication-divergence, forest-fire, adaptive coevolution, and activity-driven temporal networks — distinguishable by emitted structural metrics and by eye in the animations.

executive.what_is_this: A catalog investigation: eight studies, each a different network-reconfiguring rule implemented as a process-bigraph reaction on a shared graph substrate, each with an evolving-network animation and GIF.
executive.verdict: One generalized process reproduces all 8 Family-A dynamics; Family B runs a real SBML Repressilator (via viva-copasi) at every node with inter-node diffusion; and Family C runs that reaction–diffusion ON a topology the process is itself reconfiguring — growing or rewiring — so topology and node state co-evolve.
executive.verdict_detail: All 8 Family-A studies pass: ER stays hub-free and connected; BA and fitness build dominant hubs with heavy tails; WS and adaptive conserve edges while reorganising; duplication-divergence reproduces heavy-tailed, clustered (and fragmenting) topology; forest-fire densifies; activity-driven stays sparse and blinking. The architecture is one process + a pluggable reaction registry. Family B adds continuous multi-species dynamics ON the network: a COPASI/SBML Repressilator per node with Fickian protein transport along edges — coupled oscillators synchronise (across-node spread → 0) while the uncoupled control retains its spread. All 10 studies pass their checks. Family C closes the loop: the SBML reactors + transport run WHILE a Family-A reaction reshapes the graph. On a continuously-rewired ring the oscillators synchronise fully; on a forest-fire-grown network most newcomers entrain while weakly-attached nodes lag (topology-dependent synchronisability). All 12 studies pass. Three follow-up directions are recorded as proposed studies (13–15): quorum-sensing coupling, a model-agnostic Brusselator node reactor, and SBML-state-driven adaptive coevolution.

decisions_needed.question: Build out the proposed follow-ups (studies 13–15)?
decisions_needed.context: Families A/B/C are complete and green (12 studies). Three proposed studies — quorum-sensing coupling, a model-agnostic Brusselator swap, and SBML-state-driven adaptive coevolution — are scoped (status: planned, seeded from studies 09/11/07) as the next extensions.

scientific_argument.main_claim: Classic network-dynamics models — and continuous reaction–diffusion dynamics running ON them, even while the topology itself changes — are all special cases of one generalized, reaction-driven process-bigraph composite.
evidence_for: All 8 rules run end-to-end as process-bigraph _add/_remove structural reactions on a shared node/edge substrate.
Each study's structural signature matches theory: BA/fitness hubs (max degree ≫ mean), WS/adaptive edge conservation, forest-fire densification, activity-driven sparsity.
Adding a new dynamic is a single registered reaction function — demonstrated by the breadth of the catalog.

Family B places a real COPASI/SBML Repressilator at every node (reusing viva-copasi) and couples them by edge diffusion; coupling synchronises the oscillators (across-node spread → 0) vs the uncoupled control.

Family C runs the SBML reactors + transport ON a topology a Family-A reaction is simultaneously reconfiguring (growing or rewiring): the rewiring ring synchronises fully, the growing network mostly entrains — the dynamics OF and ON the network co-evolve in one composite.
evidence_against: The power-law exponent MLE is biased low at N≈60 (finite-size); precise exponents need far larger graphs.
Rules are faithful minimal implementations, not exhaustive variants (e.g. no non-linear PA, no aging).
caveats: Metrics are single-seed per study (seed 7); trends are robust but not ensemble-averaged.

studies.name: 01-erdos-renyi-random-growth
studies.title: Erdős–Rényi random growth
studies.question: What topology emerges when edges form purely at random, with no preference?

findings.name: erdos_renyi-signature
findings.summary: Random growth produces a homogeneous, hub-free network (Poisson-like degrees) — the null baseline the structured rules are read against.
findings.detail: Random growth gives a connected but hub-free graph; the degree spread is narrow, establishing the null against which preferential attachment's hubs stand out.

studies.claim: Random growth produces a homogeneous, hub-free network (Poisson-like degrees) — the null baseline the structured rules are read against.

derived.insight: Random growth produces a homogeneous, hub-free network (Poisson-like degrees) — the null baseline the structured rules are read against.

studies.name: 02-preferential-attachment
studies.title: Barabási–Albert preferential attachment
studies.question: Does degree-proportional attachment produce scale-free hubs?

findings.name: preferential_attachment-signature
findings.summary: Degree-proportional attachment produces scale-free hubs with a power-law degree tail — unlike random growth.
findings.detail: A clear hub emerges and the degree distribution is heavy-tailed, in contrast to the Erdős–Rényi baseline — the signature of preferential attachment. At N≈60 the maximum-likelihood exponent (γ≈1.5) is biased below the asymptotic BA value of 3, a known finite-size effect; the robust, scale-independent signal is that the maximum degree is several times the mean (vs the narrow Erdős–Rényi spread).

studies.claim: Degree-proportional attachment produces scale-free hubs with a power-law degree tail — unlike random growth.

derived.insight: Degree-proportional attachment produces scale-free hubs with a power-law degree tail — unlike random growth.

studies.name: 03-small-world-rewiring
studies.title: Watts–Strogatz small-world rewiring
studies.question: How does random rewiring of a ring lattice change its structure?

findings.name: small_world_rewire-signature
findings.summary: Random rewiring of a ring lattice preserves edge count while shortcuts collapse path length — producing the small-world regime.
findings.detail: Edge and node counts stay fixed while rewired shortcuts cross the ring — the hallmark of the Watts–Strogatz construction. The circular layout makes each rewire visible as a chord.

studies.claim: Random rewiring of a ring lattice preserves edge count while shortcuts collapse path length — producing the small-world regime.

derived.insight: Random rewiring of a ring lattice preserves edge count while shortcuts collapse path length — producing the small-world regime.

studies.name: 04-fitness-condensation
studies.title: Bianconi–Barabási fitness attachment
studies.question: Can an intrinsic node fitness let a latecomer overtake older, higher-degree nodes?

findings.name: fitness_attachment-signature
findings.summary: Fitness-weighted attachment still builds hubs, but a high-fitness latecomer can overtake older nodes — unlike pure Barabási–Albert.
findings.detail: Hubs emerge as in BA, but the leading hub's identity is fitness-driven rather than purely age-driven — the fit-get-richer effect.

studies.claim: Fitness-weighted attachment still builds hubs, but a high-fitness latecomer can overtake older nodes — unlike pure Barabási–Albert.

derived.insight: Fitness-weighted attachment still builds hubs, but a high-fitness latecomer can overtake older nodes — unlike pure Barabási–Albert.

studies.name: 05-duplication-divergence
studies.title: Duplication–divergence (biological growth)
studies.question: Does genome-style duplication-and-divergence reproduce protein-network topology?

findings.name: duplication_divergence-signature
findings.summary: Copy-then-diverge growth reproduces the heavy-tailed, locally clustered topology seen in protein-interaction networks.
findings.detail: Duplication reinforces hubs while the shared-neighbour mechanism raises clustering above a random graph — the combination that distinguishes biological growth from BA.

studies.claim: Copy-then-diverge growth reproduces the heavy-tailed, locally clustered topology seen in protein-interaction networks.

derived.insight: Copy-then-diverge growth reproduces the heavy-tailed, locally clustered topology seen in protein-interaction networks.

studies.name: 06-forest-fire-densification
studies.title: Forest-fire growth & densification
studies.question: Does recursive forest-fire burning densify the network over time?

findings.name: forest_fire-signature
findings.summary: Forest-fire growth densifies the network: mean degree rises as the graph grows, reproducing the densification law.
findings.detail: Mean degree climbs as the graph grows — the densification signature Leskovec et al. identified, which random and BA growth (fixed edges-per-node) do not show.

studies.claim: Forest-fire growth densifies the network: mean degree rises as the graph grows, reproducing the densification law.

derived.insight: Forest-fire growth densifies the network: mean degree rises as the graph grows, reproducing the densification law.

studies.name: 07-adaptive-coevolution
studies.title: Adaptive coevolution (opinions + rewiring)
studies.question: When topology and node state co-adapt, does the network organise into like-minded communities?

findings.name: adaptive_rewire-signature
findings.summary: Coevolving opinions and rewiring self-organise the network into like-minded clusters — topology and state adapt to each other.
findings.detail: Node and edge counts stay fixed while the blue/orange opinions segregate into like-minded neighbourhoods — the coevolutionary self-organisation Gross & Blasius review, and the natural bridge to dynamics-on-networks (Family B).

studies.claim: Coevolving opinions and rewiring self-organise the network into like-minded clusters — topology and state adapt to each other.

derived.insight: Coevolving opinions and rewiring self-organise the network into like-minded clusters — topology and state adapt to each other.

studies.name: 08-activity-driven-temporal
studies.title: Activity-driven temporal network
studies.question: What does an activity-driven contact sequence look like, where edges last only one time window?

findings.name: activity_driven-signature
findings.summary: Activity-driven firing produces a sparse, blinking temporal network — each snapshot is instantaneous, unlike the accreting Family-A graphs.
findings.detail: Each snapshot is a sparse, blinking contact graph rather than an accreting structure — the temporal-network view that complements the growth and rewire families.

studies.claim: Activity-driven firing produces a sparse, blinking temporal network — each snapshot is instantaneous, unlike the accreting Family-A graphs.

derived.insight: Activity-driven firing produces a sparse, blinking temporal network — each snapshot is instantaneous, unlike the accreting Family-A graphs.

studies.name: 09-sbml-nodes-coupled
studies.title: SBML reactors on a network — diffusive coupling synchronises
studies.question: When a continuous SBML oscillator runs at every node and species diffuse along the edges, does the network synchronise?

findings.name: repressilator_network_coupled-result
findings.summary: With an SBML Repressilator at each node and protein diffusion along the edges, the coupled oscillators synchronise — across-node concentration spread collapses.
findings.detail: Nine Repressilators, one per ring node, each integrated by COPASI (via viva-copasi) and coupled by protein diffusion along the edges. Starting at different phases, the oscillators entrain: the across-node PX spread collapses from its initial value toward zero while the mean keeps oscillating — reaction–diffusion synchronisation on a network. This is the headline Family-B capability: continuous, multi-species dynamics ON an evolving network with inter-node transport.

studies.claim: With an SBML Repressilator at each node and protein diffusion along the edges, the coupled oscillators synchronise — across-node concentration spread collapses.

derived.insight: With an SBML Repressilator at each node and protein diffusion along the edges, the coupled oscillators synchronise — across-node concentration spread collapses.

studies.name: 10-sbml-nodes-uncoupled
studies.title: SBML reactors on a network — uncoupled control (no diffusion)
studies.question: With diffusion switched off, do the per-node oscillators stay out of phase?

findings.name: repressilator_network_uncoupled-result
findings.summary: With diffusion off, the per-node oscillators remain independent and out of phase — the control that isolates coupling as the cause of synchronisation in study 09.
findings.detail: The same ring of Repressilators with diffusion disabled (D=0). Seeded at different phases, the nodes relax onto the common limit cycle (so the across-node spread dips from its initial transient value) but never phase-lock: a substantial spread persists (late across-node PX std ≈ 50), in sharp contrast to the coupled case where it collapses to ≈0. This control confirms the synchronisation in study 09 is caused by inter-node transport, not by the shared model.

studies.claim: With diffusion off, the per-node oscillators remain independent and out of phase — the control that isolates coupling as the cause of synchronisation in study 09.

derived.insight: With diffusion off, the per-node oscillators remain independent and out of phase — the control that isolates coupling as the cause of synchronisation in study 09.

studies.name: 11-coevolving-growing-network
studies.title: Dynamics on a growing network — reactors entrain as the graph is built
studies.question: Can SBML reactor dynamics run on a network whose topology is itself being built by a process-bigraph reaction, and do newcomers entrain?

findings.name: growing_repressilator_network-result
findings.summary: Continuous SBML dynamics run correctly on a network being built node-by-node by a PBG reaction: the system stays bounded and oscillating, and most newcomers entrain through the dense local coupling — but synchronisability is topology-dependent, with weakly-attached (low-degree) nodes lagging the synchronised core.
findings.detail: The headline synthesis: a forest-fire growth reaction builds the network node-by-node WHILE a COPASI/SBML Repressilator runs in every node and proteins diffuse along the (changing) edges. Each newcomer arrives at its own limit-cycle phase; the dense local coupling pulls most of them into the synchronised core, so the across-node spread stays small relative to the oscillation amplitude even as the network grows. Synchronisability is topology-dependent, though: a newcomer that attaches with only a single edge couples weakly and lags (Rodrigues et al. 2016). This is the companion to the uniform-degree rewiring study (12), which synchronises fully. Topology (dynamics OF the network) and continuous multi-species node state (dynamics ON the network) co-evolve in one process-bigraph composite.

studies.claim: Continuous SBML dynamics run correctly on a network being built node-by-node by a PBG reaction: the system stays bounded and oscillating, and most newcomers entrain through the dense local coupling — but synchronisability is topology-dependent, with weakly-attached (low-degree) nodes lagging the synchronised core.

derived.insight: Continuous SBML dynamics run correctly on a network being built node-by-node by a PBG reaction: the system stays bounded and oscillating, and most newcomers entrain through the dense local coupling — but synchronisability is topology-dependent, with weakly-attached (low-degree) nodes lagging the synchronised core.

studies.name: 12-coevolving-rewiring-network
studies.title: Dynamics on a rewiring network — synchrony survives continual rewiring
studies.question: Do the coupled oscillators stay synchronised when the very edges that couple them are continuously rewired?

findings.name: rewiring_repressilator_network-result
findings.summary: Coupled SBML oscillators synchronise and stay synchronised even as the coupling edges are continuously rewired — reaction–diffusion is robust to an evolving (but well-connected) topology.
findings.detail: The same 12 reactors on a ring whose edges are continuously small-world-rewired while the oscillators run (node and edge counts conserved, only the wiring changes). Because rewiring preserves connectivity and degree, the coupling stays effective: the oscillators reach and hold synchrony (across-node spread → 0) despite the topology never standing still — the companion to the growing-network study.

studies.claim: Coupled SBML oscillators synchronise and stay synchronised even as the coupling edges are continuously rewired — reaction–diffusion is robust to an evolving (but well-connected) topology.

derived.insight: Coupled SBML oscillators synchronise and stay synchronised even as the coupling edges are continuously rewired — reaction–diffusion is robust to an evolving (but well-connected) topology.

studies.name: 13-quorum-sensing-coupling
studies.title: Quorum-sensing coupling (proposed)
studies.question: Does coupling through a single diffusible signal molecule synchronise the networked reactors as effectively as diffusing the internal proteins?

studies.name: 14-brusselator-model-agnostic
studies.title: Model-agnostic node reactor — Brusselator (proposed)
studies.question: Is the SBML-at-nodes architecture model-agnostic — does swapping the Repressilator for a Brusselator reproduce reaction–diffusion patterning on the network with no code change?

studies.name: 15-sbml-adaptive-coevolution
studies.title: SBML-driven adaptive coevolution (proposed)
studies.question: When the continuous node state (an SBML readout) itself drives the rewiring, does a self-organised modular topology emerge?
